gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step is the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_ring survey reviewable without claiming a transport implementation.

The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status negotiation, feature negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, so the ring survey should build on that real foothold instead of pretending those core-side capabilities are still missing.

A dedicated survey gate keeps the live queue-discipline packet and the parked MMIO lifecycle-and-IRQ blocker explicit now that the repo has both the core slice and the first ring-local helper, so the lane can track the current reviewable boundary honestly.

The lane needs a Phase 10 note that records the landed MMIO helper ladder, the remaining blocked MMIO lifecycle-and-IRQ boundary against the roadmap, and the current parked posture without overstating virtio_ring progress.

The first honest virtio_ring step is now landed as a tiny in-memory helper for queue index, descriptor count, split or packed layout metadata, and notification bookkeeping that mirrors only the smallest reviewable shape from virtio_ring.c.

The live ring slice now adds a tiny in-memory used-buffer polling helper that reports only newly consumed chains since the previous poll, which keeps queue-lifecycle review moving without claiming interrupts, DMA, or real descriptor memory.

The live ring slice already includes a tiny callback disable helper that flips queue-local callback state off and reports whether already-consumed chains still require a follow-up poll, so the survey packet should name that landed queue-discipline surface explicitly instead of leaving disable-side bookkeeping implied.

The live ring slice now adds a tiny callback re-enable helper that flips queue-local callback state back on and reports whether already-consumed chains still need a follow-up poll before any interrupt-facing work is claimed.

The live ring slice now adds a tiny callback enable-prepare helper plus a queue-local poll snapshot that mirrors the bounded `virtqueue_enable_cb_prepare()` and `virtqueue_poll()` race check in memory, so callback re-enable discipline no longer depends only on the older last-polled bookkeeping.

The live ring slice now includes one tiny delayed-callback pacing helper that mirrors the bounded `virtqueue_enable_cb_delayed()` threshold shape in memory, so the queue-local prerequisite for the first MMIO register-window step is now satisfied without claiming interrupt delivery or event-index writes.

The live ring slice now includes a tiny notify-prepare helper that mirrors the bounded `virtqueue_kick_prepare()` `num_added` flow in memory and flushes that bookkeeping before the 16-bit counter can wrap silently, so the survey no longer has to imply that notification bookkeeping landed without a matching manifest record.

The live ring slice now includes a tiny queue-reset guard helper that reports unpublished chains, outstanding used work, and follow-up poll debt before reset, so queue discipline no longer permits in-memory resets that would drop unfinished virtqueue state.

The live ring slice now includes a tiny drained-queue reset helper that clears avail, used, callback, and notify bookkeeping while preserving queue shape metadata, so the lane records the landed in-memory reset path without claiming transport-backed or DMA-facing reset execution.

The live ring slice now includes a tiny broken-queue recovery helper that reuses the drained reset discipline after a bounded broken-queue marker, so the survey records teardown-safe queue reuse without claiming transport-backed reset execution, descriptor reclamation, or IRQ delivery.

With queue shape, used-buffer polling, callback re-enable, callback enable-prepare snapshots, delayed-callback pacing, notify-prepare bookkeeping, and queue-reset guard plus reset discipline landed, the first honest bounded MMIO follow-up was the register-window helper rather than more queue-local work.

With the register-window helper landed, the repo now also carries queue select, queue size bounds, and ready-state bookkeeping in the bounded MMIO helper, so the older queue-register step no longer belongs in ready-next posture.

Once queue select, queue size, and ready-state bookkeeping were reviewable in memory, the next bounded MMIO step was the landed queue-notify snapshot helper rather than a still-missing transport rung.

With queue-notify bookkeeping now reviewable, the live helper can also carry the landed version-scoped queue-address planning step around legacy PFN versus modern DESC, AVAIL, and USED register windows without claiming queue setup, shared interrupt delivery, or lifecycle parity.

With queue-address planning now landed, the next honest bounded MMIO follow-up was a tiny config-window snapshot helper, and the live helper now records read-only config-window snapshots against the current config-generation without claiming config writes, queue setup, IRQ delivery, or lifecycle glue.

After bounded config-window snapshots landed, the live MMIO helper now also carries a tiny config-write planning helper that records previous and planned values for byte, halfword, and word config-window rewrites while keeping config-generation explicit and without claiming full config-space parity, queue setup, IRQ delivery, probe, or remove lifecycle work.

With bounded interrupt-state summaries already landed, the live MMIO helper now also records explicit interrupt-status acknowledge bookkeeping for the reviewable queue and config interrupt bits, keeping the in-memory clear path separate from shared IRQ delivery or lifecycle claims.

Broader `virtio_mmio.c` parity still mixes interrupt acknowledgement, queue setup, queue notify side effects, config-space writes, reset, and probe or remove lifecycle paths, which remain too transport-facing to claim even after the bounded register-window, queue-register, queue-notify, queue-address, config-window, config-write, and interrupt-ack helpers are landed.
A dedicated slice note keeps the new lab helper honest about what is implemented and what still remains blocked in drivers/virtio/virtio_ring.c work.
